test_name: Comprehensive tissue NGS with KRAS A59T variant allele fraction, full extended RAS coverage (KRAS/NRAS exons 2/3/4, HRAS), and explicit BRAF V600 (FoundationOne CDx, Tempus xT CDx, Caris MI Cancer Seek, or equivalent FDA-cleared comprehensive panel)
tissue_type: archival FFPE (resected liver metastasis or primary)
rationale: A59 substitutions are recognized RAS-pathway activating alterations and current NCCN/ESMO consensus treats them as resistance variants for anti-EGFR therapy, but a single case report showed panitumumab response in an A59T tumor (pmid:30538852), so a clean VAF and a fully-resolved extended RAS plus BRAF V600 status are the only way to scope cetuximab/panitumumab and BEACON (encorafenib + cetuximab) eligibility. The same panel returns ERBB2 amplification, MSI by NGS, TMB in mut/Mb, and the PIK3CA/APC/TP53/SMAD4 confirmations downstream rows depend on. Skipping this leaves five downstream gates unresolved and forces every line discussion to hedge on RAS pathway status.
tissue_required_estimate: 1 FFPE block or 15-20 unstained slides; archival acceptable from the resected liver metastasis or the primary
decision_gated: Anti-EGFR (cetuximab, panitumumab) and BEACON (encorafenib + cetuximab) eligibility; resolves the dominant first-question gate on systemic-therapy options.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: FDA-approved companion diagnostic across mCRC therapeutic decisions including ERBB2, BRAF V600E, RAS, MSI and TMB; the most defensible single send-out for this case.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: FDA-approved 648-gene panel with CRC CDx claims; reasonable alternative if Tempus is already in-network.

providers.name: Caris Life Sciences
providers.notes: FDA-approved pan-tumor CDx with WES + WTS; useful when CMS classification is also wanted off the same block.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Diagnostic Molecular Pathology
providers.notes: Academic CAP-accredited option for centers already routed through MSK.

notes: Order this panel first; a single comprehensive NGS resolves the KRAS A59T VAF, NRAS/HRAS, BRAF V600, ERBB2 amplification, MSI, TMB, PIK3CA M1043I, APC E1295, TP53 R273 substitution, and SMAD4 R361H. Multiple downstream essential rows depend on this single send-out.

test_name: HER2 (ERBB2) IHC (clone 4B5 or HercepTest) with reflex dual-probe FISH per MOUNTAINEER / HERACLES scoring
tissue_type: archival FFPE (resected liver metastasis or primary)
rationale: MOUNTAINEER (NCT03043313) showed tucatinib + trastuzumab gives 38.1% ORR with 12.4 mo median DOR in chemotherapy-refractory HER2+ RAS-wild-type mCRC and led to the 2023 accelerated approval; HER2 amplification covers another 3-5% of mCRC and is the single most-actionable target check not yet done in this case (pmid:39058319). Standard mCRC scoring uses HERACLES criteria: IHC 3+ in >50% of cells, or IHC 2+ with HER2:CEP17 ratio >=2.0 by FISH (pmid:27108243). NGS-detected ERBB2 amplification from the comprehensive panel is acceptable per NCCN but IHC + FISH is the historically-defensible reference call, especially because anti-EGFR consideration depends on the answer. KRAS A59T status interacts with this gate because tucatinib + trastuzumab is RAS-wild-type-only.
decision_gated: Tucatinib + trastuzumab (MOUNTAINEER label), trastuzumab deruxtecan off-label, HERACLES regimens, and MOUNTAINEER-03 first-line study (NCT05253651).

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Routinely scores mCRC HER2 by HERACLES criteria; CAP-accredited and the most experienced commercial lab for the MOUNTAINEER eligibility question.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Academic reference with explicit MOUNTAINEER-context interpretation.

notes: If the comprehensive NGS already returns ERBB2 amplification with high confidence, IHC + FISH can still be added as the labeled HERACLES-style call for trial enrollment. Order the IHC first; FISH only needs to run if the IHC is 2+ equivocal.

test_name: TP53 R273 specific amino acid substitution from comprehensive tumor NGS (R273H vs R273C vs R273L vs R273S vs R273P)
tissue_type: shared with the comprehensive NGS block
rationale: R273H, R273C and R273L behave differently for the structural / chaperone p53-reactivator class: R273H and R273C have the strongest preclinical APR-246 / eprenetapopt and arsenic-trioxide reactivation data, R273L is intermediate, and R273S is a less-studied DNA-contact variant (pmid:35637218, pmid:30178893). The PYNNACLE rezatapopt study (NCT04585750) is Y220C-restricted, so this row does not by itself open PYNNACLE; it gates eprenetapopt + pembrolizumab activity and informs synthetic-lethal ATR/WEE1-class trial selection downstream. Resolving the substitution is essentially free since the comprehensive NGS already calls it; not doing so leaves the p53-axis discussion at the wrong resolution.
decision_gated: p53-reactivator-class trial selection (eprenetapopt + pembrolizumab NCT04383938; arsenic-trioxide repurposing studies); rules in or out the Y220C-restricted PYNNACLE rezatapopt study.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.assay_brand: FoundationOne CDx (TP53 codon 273 amino acid call)
providers.notes: Same block as the master NGS; substitution call is part of the standard report.

notes: Bundle with the master comprehensive NGS order; no separate send-out required. Note the specific substitution explicitly on the requisition so the report does not abbreviate to a generic 'p.R273' call.

test_name: MMR protein immunohistochemistry panel (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) plus NGS-derived MSIsensor / MANTIS score
tissue_type: archival FFPE (resected liver metastasis or primary)
rationale: MSS by single-method assay misses the rare but real discordant case where NGS-MSI or IHC alone calls a tumor MSS that the orthogonal method calls MSI-H (overall concordance ~95%, discordance ~5%, pmid:31416808). Confirming MSS by both NGS MSIsensor and four-antibody MMR IHC closes the door on tumor-agnostic ICI definitively rather than presumptively, which matters because MSI-H mCRC has a 44% ORR with pembrolizumab and would reorder the entire decision tree. The IHC is a low-cost defensive call that the comprehensive NGS does not substitute for.
turnaround_estimate: 5-7 business days for MMR IHC; NGS-MSI is on the master panel turnaround
tissue_required_estimate: 1-2 unstained slides for the four-antibody MMR panel
decision_gated: Single-agent and dual-agent ICI (pembrolizumab, dostarlimab, nivolumab + ipilimumab); reverses entire treatment paradigm if MSI-H by either method.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Widely-used commercial CAP-accredited MMR IHC; the standard orthogonal call alongside NGS-MSI.

notes: Add the MMR IHC requisition to the same FFPE block used for the comprehensive NGS so a single block release covers both. NGS-MSI is bundled with the master panel and does not need a separate order.

test_name: TMB calculation from the comprehensive NGS report, expressed in mutations per megabase with the panel's definition and threshold documented
tissue_type: shared with the master NGS block
rationale: The tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab label requires TMB >=10 mut/Mb on FoundationOne CDx; the intake says 'TMB-low' without the numeric value, and a value of 8-9 mut/Mb would close the door while 10-12 would open it. Each panel uses a slightly different bait region and counting rule (FoundationOne CDx 0.8 Mb of CDS; Tempus xT 595 Mb captured / 2.4 Mb reportable; MSK-IMPACT 1.06 Mb), so the panel and threshold need to travel with the number (pmid:32826381). Without the explicit value, every downstream ICI discussion is blocked from being either approved or trial-eligible.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: The FDA-labeled TMB-H call for pembrolizumab uses FoundationOne CDx specifically; other panels report TMB but the label cites this assay.

notes: Bundled with the master NGS; the action item is to make sure the report explicitly states the mut/Mb number and the panel definition, not just 'low' or 'high'.

test_name: PD-L1 IHC with explicit clone (22C3, SP263, or 28-8) and explicit scoring system (CPS for mCRC; TPS or IC if a thoracic-context comparison is needed)
rationale: 'Negative' without a clone or scoring system is not interpretable for trial eligibility because different ICI labels and combination studies use different cutoffs and antibodies (e.g. 22C3 CPS for pembrolizumab, SP263 TPS for atezolizumab; pmid:30604034). Several MSS-mCRC combination ICI trials use PD-L1 CPS thresholds for stratification rather than for hard exclusion, so the exact CPS value still matters even when the headline result is negative. Re-staining is cheap; reordering the entire combination-ICI conversation around an ambiguous call is not.
decision_gated: ICI combination trial stratification and any PD-L1-conditioned MSS-CRC ICI regimen.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Runs all three FDA-approved clones with explicit CPS / TPS / IC scoring; the operationally simplest order for getting a clone + scoring system both documented.

notes: Ask the requisition to default to 22C3 with CPS scoring for CRC context; add SP263 only if a thoracic-context combination study comes into the trial mix.

test_name: DPYD genotyping for the four CPIC-recommended variants (c.1905+1G>A / *2A, c.1679T>G / *13, c.2846A>T, c.1236G>A / HapB3)
tissue_type: peripheral whole blood (EDTA) or buccal swab
rationale: FDA updated the 5-FU and capecitabine labels in March 2024 to advise considering DPYD testing pre-treatment, and the 2026 NCCN colon guideline now recommends discussing DPYD genotyping with all patients before fluoropyrimidine therapy (pmid:40958923). The patient is already on FOLFIRI and has tolerated cycles, which lowers but does not eliminate the value: heterozygous carriers of c.2846A>T or HapB3 can show progressive cumulative toxicity, and HIPEC-window dose decisions plus any future capecitabine maintenance both benefit from a documented genotype. Skipping it leaves a known toxicity risk unmeasured during the peri-operative window.
tissue_required_estimate: 5 mL whole blood (EDTA) or buccal swab kit
decision_gated: Fluoropyrimidine dose adjustment for ongoing FOLFIRI and any future capecitabine maintenance.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Covers all four CPIC-recommended variants; the most straightforward US clinical genotype for fluoropyrimidine safety.

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

notes: Pair with UGT1A1 on a single pharmacogenomic requisition. If the patient has already tolerated four cycles, the testing is still warranted because cumulative-toxicity carriers can compensate early and decompensate later.

test_name: UGT1A1 genotyping for *6 and *28 alleles (TA repeat polymorphism)
tissue_type: peripheral whole blood (EDTA) or buccal swab
rationale: UGT1A1 *28/*28 (and *6/*28 in Asian ancestry) confers a 3-4x increased risk of severe irinotecan-related neutropenia and diarrhea, and the FDA irinotecan label recommends a starting-dose reduction in homozygotes (pmid:21570278). The patient is already on FOLFIRI, so the value of testing now is two-fold: dose-rationalize the remaining FOLFIRI cycles if toxicity emerges, and pre-resolve the irinotecan-HIPEC question because some HIPEC protocols use intraperitoneal irinotecan. Mostly bundled with DPYD on a single pharmacogenomics order.
tissue_required_estimate: 5 mL whole blood (EDTA) or shared with DPYD order
decision_gated: Irinotecan dose adjustment in FOLFIRI and any irinotecan-based HIPEC protocol.

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Bundles with DPYD as a single pharmacogenomic send-out; the routine US clinical genotype.

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

notes: Order on the same requisition as DPYD; results inform irinotecan dose adjustment and HIPEC agent selection.

test_name: Chromosome 20q amplification segment definition (20q11.21 BCL2L1/TOP1 vs extended 20q13 ZNF217/MYBL2/AURKA) from NGS copy-number plot, with optional confirmatory FISH or OncoScan/SNP-array if the NGS boundaries are ambiguous
tissue_type: shared with the master NGS block
rationale: 20q11.21-restricted amplification centered on BCL2L1 (BCL-xL) and TOP1 is biologically distinct from broad 20q gain that sweeps in 20q13 (ZNF217, MYBL2, AURKA): the BCL2L1 subset supports BH3-mimetic / BCL-xL-degrader rationale (navitoclax, DT2216, pmid:40988632) and the TOP1 amplification correlates with irinotecan sensitivity, while the broader 20q gain raises AURKA-class trial questions instead (pmid:30139729). The comprehensive NGS already returns copy-number profiles; the action is to inspect the segment plot and confirm boundaries rather than accept the simple gene-level call. Skipping this leaves the BCL-xL-directed rationale at the wrong resolution.
decision_gated: BCL-xL-directed strategy framing (navitoclax, DT2216) and 20q13-driven AURKA-class trial framing; refines the irinotecan-sensitivity rationale on top of TOP1.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Segment-level CNV is reported on the standard FoundationOne report; same block as the master order.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Use only if NGS-CNV boundaries are ambiguous; OncoScan resolves segment edges more cleanly than panel-based CNV.

notes: No new sample needed in most cases; the action is on the interpretation of the existing CNV plot. If the NGS report flags 20q amplification without segment boundaries, request a CNV-segment annotation from the lab or reflex to OncoScan.

test_name: Tumor-informed serial ctDNA MRD assay at three peri-HIPEC timepoints (pre-CRS/HIPEC baseline, post-operative day 30-60, then every 8-12 weeks)
tissue_type: 5-10 mL plasma in Streck tubes; tumor-informed assays also need archival FFPE for assay design
rationale: Peritoneal-spread CRC is one of the settings where ctDNA MRD is most predictive: pre-CRS/HIPEC ctDNA detection correlates with shorter PFS and identifies patients who may benefit more from extended systemic therapy than from upfront cytoreduction (pmid:32576704). Signatera has Medicare coverage for stage II-IV CRC MRD surveillance and the tumor-informed bespoke design (16 patient-specific variants from WES) gives the best low-tumor-fraction sensitivity (pmid:34754095); Guardant Reveal is the tumor-naive alternative with ~81% serial-sample sensitivity. Skipping ctDNA leaves the lead-time signal for peritoneal recurrence on the table.
turnaround_estimate: Signatera bespoke build 4-6 weeks; subsequent draws 2 weeks. Guardant Reveal 2 weeks per draw.
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL plasma per draw; Signatera baseline also needs an FFPE block (can share the master NGS block)
decision_gated: Peri-HIPEC recurrence surveillance; informs adjuvant-therapy duration after cytoreductive surgery + HIPEC.

providers.name: Natera
providers.address: 13011 McCallen Pass, Building A, Austin, TX 78753
providers.notes: Medicare-covered for stage II-IV CRC; the most sensitive option for low-tumor-fraction peritoneal disease post-HIPEC. Best fit for this case.

providers.name: Guardant Health
providers.notes: Tumor-naive option; faster start because no bespoke build is needed but lower analytical sensitivity than Signatera.

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Tumor-informed alternative if the master NGS already runs through Foundation.

notes: Bracket the surgery: one baseline draw pre-CRS/HIPEC, one at post-operative day 30-60, then every 8-12 weeks. Use Signatera as the surveillance backbone and reserve Guardant360 or FoundationOne Liquid CDx for the recurrence-genotyping moment if ctDNA turns positive.

test_name: Consensus molecular subtype (CMS1-4) by transcriptomic classifier (CRCassigner / CMScaller from RNA-seq) plus CDX2 IHC and ZEB1/HTR2B/FRMD6/cytokeratin IHC panel as the surrogate when RNA-seq is not available
rationale: Peritoneal-dominant disease with SMAD4 loss raises the prior for CMS4 (mesenchymal) classification, which has a worse prognosis but identifies patients with a TGF-beta-mediated immune-excluded phenotype and a different combination-therapy landscape than CMS2/3 (pmid:41276825, pmid:38658912). The IHC surrogate panel (CDX2, ZEB1, HTR2B, FRMD6, pan-cytokeratin) achieves 87% concordance with transcriptomic CMS and is the practical clinical-lab path when full RNA-seq is unavailable. Result reframes ICI-combination, TGF-beta-axis, and stromal-targeting trial selection rather than gating a specific drug today.
turnaround_estimate: RNA-seq 3-4 weeks; IHC surrogate 5-7 business days
tissue_required_estimate: archival FFPE; 5-10 unstained slides for IHC surrogate
decision_gated: TGF-beta-axis / mesenchymal-targeting trial selection; CMS4 prognostic stratification; CDX2-negative HR-poor subgroup identification.

providers.name: Caris Life Sciences
providers.assay_brand: MI Cancer Seek (WES + WTS, CMS classification on whole-transcriptome RNA)
providers.notes: Whole-transcriptome RNA on the same comprehensive order; the most efficient way to add a transcriptomic CMS call when MI Cancer Seek is already in play.

providers.name: Tempus Labs
providers.notes: Whole-transcriptome RNA; CMS call available on request.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.assay_brand: CDX2 IHC (plus ZEB1, HTR2B, FRMD6, pan-cytokeratin for the IHC-CMS surrogate)
providers.notes: IHC surrogate is the right fallback when RNA-seq is impractical.

notes: Best value if Caris MI Cancer Seek is already used as the master comprehensive panel since CMS comes off the whole-transcriptome data. The IHC surrogate (CDX2 plus the four-marker panel) is the practical fallback otherwise.

test_name: High-resolution HLA-A typing (4-digit, exon 2/3/4 resolution) plus full class-I and class-II profile if downstream TCR-T or ImmTAC trials are in scope
rationale: MSS / TMB-low mCRC is exactly the population where HLA-restricted TCR-T and ImmTAC (soluble TCR) trials are most often considered: HLA-A*02:01 is the dominant restriction for MAGE-A4 (afami-cel), NY-ESO-1 (lete-cel), PRAME (IMA203, brenetafusp) and several CRC-adjacent constructs (pmid:38843780). High-resolution four-digit typing on blood is the standard pre-screen; without it, every TCR-T or ImmTAC referral starts over. Not currently approved for CRC but actively-enrolling trials make this worth banking now while peri-HIPEC pause windows allow it.
decision_gated: HLA-restricted TCR-T (afami-cel, lete-cel, IMA203) and ImmTAC / soluble-TCR (brenetafusp, IMC-P115C) trial eligibility.

providers.name: Labcorp
providers.assay_brand: HLA A, B, C, DRB1 Profile (High Resolution)
providers.notes: Most widely-accessible US clinical lab offering 4-digit class-I + class-II HLA; what most TCR-T trial central labs accept for the pre-screen.

providers.name: Histogenetics
providers.assay_brand: HLA Class I/II High-Resolution Sanger / NGS Typing
providers.notes: Specialty lab; the central typing lab for many transplant and TCR-T programs.

providers.name: American Red Cross National Histocompatibility Laboratory
providers.address: 700 Spring Forest Road, Suite 300, Raleigh, NC 27609

notes: Bank the result before the HIPEC procedure if at all possible; even if no TCR-T trial is in immediate play, the result lasts for life and removes friction from any future TCR-T referral.

test_name: SMAD4 (DPC4) IHC (clone B-8 or EP618Y) on archival FFPE
rationale: R361H sits in the MH2 DNA-binding domain and is a known loss-of-function hotspot; SMAD4 IHC loss is the protein-level orthogonal confirmation that the molecular call actually translates to absent nuclear SMAD4 (pmid:24798147, pmid:32531298). Confirms the SMAD4-loss phenotype that anchors the CMS4-mesenchymal hypothesis and any TGF-beta-axis trial discussion. Cheap defensive call rather than a gating one because the molecular evidence is already strong.
decision_gated: Confirms SMAD4-loss phenotype underpinning CMS4 / mesenchymal interpretation and TGF-beta-axis trial discussion.

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Commercial CAP-accredited SMAD4 stain; pair with the MMR IHC order on the same block.

notes: Bundle with the MMR IHC and SMAD4 stain on a single requisition to avoid a separate block release.

test_name: Exact APC codon-1295 variant type and position relative to the mutation cluster region (MCR), with second-allele status (loss of heterozygosity vs second truncating event) from the comprehensive NGS report
rationale: Codon 1295 sits within the APC mutation cluster region (codons 1250-1500); truncating events in the MCR retain partial beta-catenin binding but lose the SAMP repeats needed for downregulation, and bi-allelic MCR truncation is the typical 'just right' Wnt-pathway state most studied for Wnt-axis drug rationale (pmid:18327014, pmid:30425174). The variant call (E1295* nonsense vs frameshift vs missense) and the second-allele status decide whether this case is a strong candidate for Wnt-pathway investigational trials (PORCN inhibitors, tankyrase inhibitors, frizzled antibodies) or a weak one. Useful for refining trial fit, not currently gating an approved therapy.
decision_gated: Wnt-axis investigational trial fit (PORCN, tankyrase, frizzled / WNT974 / LGK974-class).

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Variant call and second-allele status on the standard report; same block as the master NGS order.

notes: No new sample needed; the action is on the interpretation. Request the lab to explicitly call the variant type (nonsense / frameshift / missense) and the second-allele state, both of which sit in the raw VCF but are sometimes summarized.

test_name: Serum CEA, CA 19-9, and CA 125 at baseline and at each peri-HIPEC interval (every 4-8 weeks during therapy; pre-CRS, day 30, then with each surveillance imaging)
rationale: Peritoneal-spread CRC is the setting where CA 125 adds the most to the standard CEA / CA 19-9 panel; CA 125 elevation correlates with peritoneal carcinomatosis burden and tracks response and recurrence independently of CEA (pmid:25223358). Together they give a low-cost peri-HIPEC response signal that complements ctDNA and imaging. Skipping them leaves the routine biochemical recurrence signal untracked, especially in CA 19-9-secreting subtypes that the FOLFIRI may suppress unevenly.
decision_gated: Peri-HIPEC biochemical surveillance; CA 125 specifically tracks peritoneal-disease burden.

providers.name: Quest Diagnostics
providers.notes: Universally available at draw stations; bundle the three markers on one requisition.

notes: Pull all three at every routine draw rather than CEA alone; the marginal cost is negligible and CA 125 is the disproportionately useful signal for peritoneal-burden tracking.

test_name: Explicit confirmation that there is no co-occurring TP53 Y220C variant on the comprehensive NGS report
rationale: Most TP53-mutant CRC tumors carry a single dominant TP53 alteration; the intake reports R273 only. The PYNNACLE rezatapopt study (NCT04585750) requires a TP53 Y220C mutation as the binding pocket the drug exploits, and the trial additionally requires KRAS wild-type which this case fails, so this is a low-probability rule-out rather than a likely gate. Still cheap to confirm there is no second hit at Y220C from the existing NGS report.
decision_gated: PYNNACLE / rezatapopt eligibility rule-out (case is KRAS-mutant so likely excluded regardless).

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: Confirmation comes from re-reading the existing NGS report; no new send-out needed.

notes: Read off the existing comprehensive NGS report; no separate order. Listed as a low-priority row because the case is KRAS-mutant and PYNNACLE is KRAS-wild-type-restricted, but the rule-out should be documented explicitly so the trial screener does not waste time on it.

test_name: Spatial / multiplex immune profile of TIL density, CD3/CD8 distribution, FAP+ stromal CAF density, and pSMAD2/3 in the peritumoral stroma (multiplex IHC or Akoya/Lunaphore platform)
rationale: SMAD4 loss plus a CMS4-mesenchymal phenotype is the canonical TGF-beta-driven immune-excluded state, where CD8+ T cells are stuck at the invasive margin behind a FAP+ CAF stromal collar (pmid:29670281). A multiplex immune-microenvironment profile separates 'cold' (truly absent TIL) from 'excluded' (TIL trapped at margin) cases, which sharpens combination-ICI trial selection (anti-TGF-beta + ICI such as bintrafusp alfa, BCA101, or NIS793-class agents). Mostly research-grade; useful for trial selection but not gating.
decision_gated: Anti-TGF-beta + ICI combination trial selection (bintrafusp alfa-class, NIS793, BCA101).

providers.name: Akoya Biosciences
providers.notes: Commercial multiplex-IHC service; the most accessible US path for clinical-grade spatial immune profiling outside academic centers.

providers.name: Memorial Sloan Kettering Pathology Translational Research Lab
providers.notes: Research-grade multiplex IHC at an NCI-designated center; better fit when a trial central lab is already routing through MSK.

notes: Reserve for the moment when a TGF-beta-axis or stromal-targeting trial enters serious discussion; not part of the immediate workup.

test_name: Documentation review of the existing negative multi-gene germline panel (Lynch genes plus APC, MUTYH, POLE/POLD1, SMAD4, BMPR1A, STK11, PTEN, CDH1, TP53) and confirmation that POLE/POLD1 and POLD1 V411L / POLE P286R proofreading hotspots were covered
rationale: The intake says the multi-gene germline panel was negative, but a 37-year-old with mCRC sits in the early-onset bracket where polymerase-proofreading deficiency (germline POLE / POLD1) is on the differential even at TMB-low (pmid:32424176). If the prior panel did not specifically cover the POLE proofreading exonuclease domain and POLD1, a focused add-on is warranted; if it did, the row is documentation only. Cheap defensive check given the patient age.
turnaround_estimate: 1 week for documentation review; 2-3 weeks for add-on testing if needed
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood (EDTA) only if add-on testing is needed
decision_gated: Polymerase-proofreading polyposis surveillance and family cascade decisions; downstream tumor-agnostic ICI rationale if POLE proofreading deficiency is uncovered.

providers.name: Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae)
providers.assay_brand: Invitae Common Hereditary Cancers Panel (POLE/POLD1 included)
providers.notes: Standard US hereditary-cancer panel that includes POLE and POLD1 proofreading-domain coverage.

notes: First action is to pull the existing germline report and confirm gene list coverage. Add-on testing for POLE / POLD1 is only needed if the original panel did not include them.
